correctness.rationale: For \(n=4p\), the published divisor reduction leaves \(C_{4p}\) as the only potentially nonintegral block. The published elementary-symmetric formula shows that the only low exceptional coefficient is at degree \(p-1\). A logarithmic coefficient extraction proves \(p^3 C_{4p}\equiv14/45\pmod p\) for every prime \(p\ge11\), while exact Newton recurrence gives \(C_{28}=-34695770811027473098809241186/49\) with numerator \(2\pmod7\). Thus every quantifier and boundary prime in the claim is covered.

value.rationale: The same-object source singles out denominator patterns and proves a prime-denominator theorem at \(2p\). The \(4p\) layer is the next natural dyadic case. The exact exponent jump to \(3\), together with the unique \(p=7\) cancellation and its mechanism in the Newton/log expansion, is a structural result rather than an arbitrary finite computation and provides a template for higher layers.
